subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose explicit native subagent child-topic session spawning now, and should that be implemented through the current core session-binding adapter capability rather than new primary `subagent_spawning` routing?
rationale: The remaining behavior affects visible Telegram topic creation, plugin/API capability shape, session routing defaults, and commentary/message exposure, which cannot be safely resolved by cleanup automation.

options.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve conflicts and review blockers, and require final-head live Telegram proof.

options.title: Defer child-topic spawning
options.body: Keep current-conversation Telegram binding only until maintainers decide the user-visible topic and API model.

options.title: Reject child-topic subagent spawning
options.body: Close this tracker and associated candidates if maintainers decide internal subagent work should not create Telegram topics.

recommendation.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve conflicts and review blockers, and require final-head live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decisive implementation boundary is the core session-binding refactor and related channel policy that steipete authored.
